s2025-161.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 46 to begin work on a resolution that would cancel newer, stricter energy efficiency standards for walk-in coolers and freezers. If passed, the resolution would remove the requirement that certain walk-in doors and refrigeration systems meet those standards.

s2025-162.name: Repealing Energy Standards for Walk-In Coolers and Freezers
s2025-162.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 42 to pass a resolution that cancels new energy-efficiency rules for walk-in coolers and freezers. Walk-in non-display doors and refrigeration systems would no longer have to meet those stricter standards.

s2025-165.name: Senate vote on blocking military sale to Israel
s2025-165.plain: The Senate voted against moving a resolution to block a proposed weapons sale to Israel out of committee, so it stays in committee for now. The vote was 15 in favor and 82 against.

s2025-166.name: Blocking a vote on arms sales to Israel
s2025-166.plain: The Senate voted 83 to 15 against pulling a resolution out of committee. The resolution would block a proposed sale of certain military equipment and services to Israel. The full Senate will not take it up at this time.

s2025-169.name: Senate Votes to Begin Work on 2025 Federal Budget Plan
s2025-169.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 48 to begin work on a budget resolution setting federal spending, revenue and deficit targets for fiscal year 2025 and the years through 2034. This step does not itself approve the budget.

s2025-170.name: Amendment to protect Medicare and Medicaid funding in budget plan
s2025-170.plain: The Senate approved a change to the 2025 budget plan that would set up a reserve fund to protect Medicare and Medicaid, with no net effect on the deficit. The vote was 51 in favor and 48 against.

s2025-171.name: Proposed limit on new debt in budget resolution
s2025-171.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the budget plan that would have blocked bills adding more debt over 30 years than the country has built up in its 249 years. The vote was 46 in favor and 53 against.

s2025-172.name: Amendment to protect Medicaid enrollment and benefits
s2025-172.plain: The Senate voted on a proposed change to the budget plan that would set aside funds to prevent cuts in Medicaid enrollment or benefits for seniors, children, families, people with disabilities, veterans and military families. The change was rejected, 48 in favor to 51 against.

s2025-173.name: Amendment to remove farm committee instructions from budget plan
s2025-173.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change that would have removed instructions for the Agriculture Committee from the budget plan, by 47 votes in favor to 51 against.

s2025-174.name: Proposed ban on sharing military operation details over messaging apps
s2025-174.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the budget resolution, 46 to 53. The change would have set aside money to ban using commercial messaging apps to send details about the timing, sequence, or weapons of upcoming U.S. military operations abroad.

s2025-175.name: Amendment to protect federal workers' union contracts
s2025-175.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the budget plan that would have set aside funds to protect federal workers' union contracts and their right to organize, by a vote of 48 in favor to 51 against.

s2025-176.name: Amendment on tariffs and grocery prices in budget plan
s2025-176.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the 2025 budget plan, 46 to 53. The change would have set aside a fund, with no added deficit, to keep tariffs from raising the cost of groceries and everyday goods for families.

s2025-177.name: Amendment on FEMA's disaster relief role
s2025-177.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the budget resolution that would have stated the importance of FEMA and its continued role in providing long-term disaster relief to survivors. The vote was 48 in favor and 51 against.

s2025-178.name: Amendment on security aid to Ukraine in budget resolution
s2025-178.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the 2025 federal budget plan, 48 to 51, that would have aimed to prevent any disruption in security assistance to Ukraine.

s2025-179.name: Proposed change to debt limit instructions in budget plan
s2025-179.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the debt limit instructions in the budget plan for fiscal year 2025, with 5 voting yes and 94 voting no. The change would have altered how much the debt limit is raised for the House and Senate.

s2025-180.name: Amendment on Social Security Administration cuts and senior services
s2025-180.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change, 49 to 50, that would have set aside money in a budget reserve fund to reverse cuts to the Social Security Administration and other senior services.

s2025-181.name: Amendment on using public land sale money for deficit reduction
s2025-181.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change that would have set aside a fund so money from public land sales could not be used to reduce the federal deficit, by 48 votes to 51.

s2025-182.name: Amendment to keep Social Security offices open
s2025-182.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the budget plan that would have barred DOGE from closing Social Security offices, keeping access to benefits for seniors and people with disabilities. The vote was 48 in favor and 51 against.

s2025-183.name: Amendment on a fund for caregivers in the budget resolution
s2025-183.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 49 to reject a proposed change to the budget resolution. The change would have created a fund, with no added deficit, to protect caregivers, including people caring for seniors and children and home care workers, from new barriers.

s2025-184.name: Amendment to allow a $17 federal minimum wage by simple majority
s2025-184.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to a federal budget resolution that would have ensured a $17-an-hour federal minimum wage could be approved by a simple majority vote. The vote was 47 in favor and 52 against.

s2025-185.name: Senate vote on Medicare drug cost rule waiver
s2025-185.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 50 on whether to set aside a budget rule that a senator said would block a measure raising drug costs for seniors and people with disabilities on Medicare. The vote needed 60 votes to pass and did not reach that number, so the rule stayed in force.

s2025-186.name: Amendment on Medicaid funding for rural hospitals
s2025-186.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 50 to reject a proposed change to a budget resolution. The change would have set aside money to prevent cuts to Medicaid that could close rural hospitals or raise costs for others.

s2025-187.name: Amendment to keep Social Security phone service
s2025-187.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the budget plan that would have preserved access to Social Security's phone service. The vote was 48 in favor and 51 against.

s2025-188.name: Amendment on a health care reserve fund for Medicaid
s2025-188.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to a budget plan that would have set aside funds to protect health care, including preventing Medicaid cuts that could reduce benefits or coverage. The vote was 48 in favor and 51 against.

s2025-189.name: Amendment to remove Medicaid spending cuts from budget plan
s2025-189.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change that would have removed instructions for House committees to cut $880 billion from Medicaid, with 49 voting yes and 50 voting no.

s2025-190.name: Proposed middle-class tax relief amendment to budget plan
s2025-190.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 52 to reject a proposed change to the budget plan that would have provided tax relief for the middle class. The change was not adopted.

s2025-191.name: Senate adopts 2025 federal budget blueprint
s2025-191.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 48 to adopt a budget framework for federal spending and revenue for 2025, with projected levels through 2034. The plan directs House committees to write laws that change the deficit and raise the debt limit.

s2025-206.name: Senate vote to take up energy efficiency rule for water heaters
s2025-206.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 42 to begin considering a measure that would overturn a Department of Energy rule setting energy efficiency standards for gas-fired instantaneous water heaters. The rule was issued in December 2024.

s2025-207.name: Overturning federal energy rule for gas water heaters
s2025-207.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 44 to pass a resolution that cancels a Department of Energy rule setting energy efficiency standards for gas-fired instantaneous water heaters, which the rule had adopted in December 2024.

s2025-222.name: Senate Starts Debate on Energy Appliance Rule Repeal
s2025-222.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 46 to begin considering a resolution that would cancel a 2024 Energy Department rule on labeling, certification and enforcement for certain appliances and industrial equipment. This was a step to begin debate, not the final vote on the resolution.

s2025-223.name: Overturning federal energy rules for appliances and equipment
s2025-223.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 46 to pass a resolution that cancels a 2024 Department of Energy rule. The rule set new certification, labeling, and enforcement requirements for energy efficiency in certain home appliances, such as washing machines and dishwashers, and in industrial equipment.

s2025-224.name: Senate vote to take up energy standards for commercial refrigerators
s2025-224.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 46 to begin considering a measure that would cancel newer, stricter energy efficiency standards for commercial refrigerators and freezers, which businesses would have had to meet by 2029.

s2025-225.name: Ending the emergency behind global tariffs
s2025-225.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 49 on a resolution to end the national emergency that was used to impose a 10% tariff on most imports and extra duties on some trading partners. Because the vote was tied, the resolution was defeated.

s2025-226.name: Senate vote to set aside tariff emergency resolution
s2025-226.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 49, with the Vice President breaking the tie, to set aside a resolution that would have ended the national emergency used to impose global tariffs. Setting it aside effectively ends it without a direct vote on the resolution itself.

s2025-227.name: Senate moves to start work on EPA air pollution rule repeal
s2025-227.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 40 to begin considering a measure that would overturn an EPA rule on how factories that release certain hazardous air pollutants are classified. This vote was only to start work on it, not a final decision on the measure.

s2025-228.name: Overturning new energy standards for commercial refrigerators and freezers
s2025-228.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 45 to pass a resolution that cancels new federal energy efficiency standards for commercial refrigerators, freezers, and refrigerator-freezers. Businesses would no longer have to meet those standards, which had been due by January 2029.

s2025-229.name: Overturning EPA rule on reclassifying major sources of air pollution
s2025-229.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 46 to pass a resolution that cancels an Environmental Protection Agency rule. The rule required facilities that reclassify from major to area sources of hazardous air pollutants to keep certain emission controls so their emissions do not increase.

s2025-231.name: Senate vote to take up rubber tire air pollution rule repeal
s2025-231.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 43 to begin considering a resolution that would overturn the Environmental Protection Agency's rule setting air pollution limits for rubber tire manufacturing, specifically for the rubber processing part of the industry. The vote began debate; it did not finally pass the resolution.

s2025-232.name: Rubber tire factory air pollution rule
s2025-232.plain: The Senate voted 55 to 45 to pass a resolution that cancels the Environmental Protection Agency's rule setting air pollution limits for the rubber processing part of tire manufacturing. The change removes those limits.

s2025-233.name: Senate Votes to Take Up Bank Merger Rule Disapproval
s2025-233.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 46 to begin work on a resolution that would cancel a federal rule changing how bank mergers are reviewed, including removing automatic approvals and streamlined application forms.

s2025-235.name: Senate Votes to Take Up Wi-Fi Hotspot Rule Repeal
s2025-235.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 47 to begin considering a resolution that would cancel a federal rule letting schools and libraries buy discounted Wi-Fi hotspots for students and patrons to use at home.

s2025-236.name: Off-road vehicle rules in Glen Canyon recreation area
s2025-236.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 47 to begin considering a measure that would overturn a National Park Service rule limiting off-road vehicles in parts of the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area. If passed, the measure would allow off-road vehicles in certain areas the rule had closed.

s2025-237.name: Reversing New Rules for Bank Merger Reviews
s2025-237.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 47 to pass a measure that cancels a new rule from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. The rule changed how bank mergers are reviewed, including removing automatic approvals and streamlined application forms.

s2025-238.name: Overturning FCC rule on school Wi-Fi hotspots
s2025-238.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 38 to pass a measure that cancels an FCC rule letting schools and libraries buy discounted Wi-Fi hotspots and mobile service for students and patrons to use off-site, mainly for educational purposes.

s2025-239.name: Off-road vehicle rules in Glen Canyon recreation area
s2025-239.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 43 to pass a resolution that cancels a National Park Service rule limiting off-road vehicles in parts of the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, which covers northern Arizona and southeastern Utah. Under the resolution, those areas could again allow off-road vehicle use.

s2025-240.name: Senate vote on starting debate on the GENIUS Act
s2025-240.plain: The Senate voted on whether to end debate and move ahead on the GENIUS Act, a bill setting rules for stablecoins, digital assets meant to hold a fixed value. The vote fell short, with 48 in favor and 49 against, and did not reach the 60 votes needed.

s2025-259.name: Request for information on El Salvador's human rights record
s2025-259.plain: The Senate voted on whether to take a resolution asking for information about El Salvador's human rights practices out of committee so the full Senate could consider it. The vote was 45 in favor and 50 against, so the resolution stays in committee.

s2025-262.name: Senate moves ahead on stablecoin regulation bill
s2025-262.plain: The Senate voted 66 to 32 to end debate and move ahead on the GENIUS Act, which sets a federal framework for payment stablecoins, digital assets that issuers must redeem for a fixed value. The 60 votes needed were reached.

s2025-263.name: Senate Votes to Begin Work on GENIUS Act
s2025-263.plain: The Senate voted 69 to 31 to start debate on the GENIUS Act, a measure to set rules for stablecoins, which are digital assets that issuers must redeem for a fixed value. This step does not yet pass the bill itself.

s2025-264.name: Senate Vote on Hydrogen Vehicle Fuel System Safety Rule
s2025-264.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 46 to begin considering a resolution that would cancel a federal safety rule on fuel storage systems in hydrogen-powered vehicles. The rule, published in January 2025, set performance requirements for hydrogen fuel systems and storage tanks.

s2025-265.name: Hydrogen vehicle fuel safety rule: Senate vote to set aside
s2025-265.plain: The Senate voted 46 to 52 against setting aside a resolution that would cancel a safety rule for hydrogen-fueled vehicles, so the resolution stays alive. The rule set performance requirements for hydrogen vehicle fuel systems and storage tanks, including how they should hold up in crashes.

s2025-266.name: Setting Aside Hydrogen Vehicle Fuel Safety Rule
s2025-266.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 46 to set aside a resolution that would have canceled a federal safety rule for hydrogen-fueled vehicles, which ends that effort without a direct vote on the resolution itself. The rule covers fuel system and hydrogen storage tank requirements for such vehicles.

s2025-267.name: Disapproval of federal hydrogen vehicle fuel safety rule
s2025-267.plain: The Senate voted on a motion to overturn a federal safety rule for hydrogen-fueled vehicles, which sets requirements for their fuel systems and hydrogen storage tanks. The motion was rejected, 46 in favor to 51 against.

s2025-268.name: Hydrogen vehicle fuel safety rule disapproval motion
s2025-268.plain: The Senate voted 45 to 51 against a motion to overturn a federal safety rule for hydrogen-powered vehicles, so the motion was rejected. The rule sets performance requirements for hydrogen fuel systems and storage tanks, including protection against leaks and bursts.

s2025-269.name: Vote on overturning hydrogen vehicle fuel safety rule
s2025-269.plain: The Senate voted 46 to 51 against a motion to overturn a federal safety rule on fuel systems and hydrogen storage in hydrogen-powered vehicles, so the motion was rejected.

s2025-270.name: Senate rejects motion on hydrogen vehicle fuel safety rule
s2025-270.plain: The Senate voted 46 to 51 to reject a motion to overturn a federal safety rule for hydrogen-powered vehicles. The rule sets fuel system and hydrogen storage tank requirements, and the motion did not pass.

s2025-271.name: Vote to overturn hydrogen vehicle fuel safety rule
s2025-271.plain: The Senate rejected a motion to overturn a federal safety rule for hydrogen-fueled vehicles, which sets fuel system and hydrogen storage tank requirements. The vote was 45 in favor and 52 against.

s2025-272.name: Vote on hydrogen vehicle safety rule
s2025-272.plain: The Senate voted 46 to 51 against a motion to adjourn, so the chamber stayed in session. The vote was not on the hydrogen vehicle safety rule itself, which would have been canceled had the resolution passed.

s2025-273.name: Senate ruling on hydrogen vehicle safety rule disapproval
s2025-273.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 46 to uphold a ruling on how its rules apply to a resolution that would undo federal safety standards for hydrogen-fueled vehicles. The ruling was made on a procedural question, not on the resolution itself.

s2025-274.name: Senate ruling on hydrogen vehicle safety rule disapproval
s2025-274.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 46 to uphold a ruling on its own rules about a resolution to overturn a 2025 federal safety rule covering hydrogen-fueled vehicles. The resolution would have nullified that rule.

s2025-275.name: Overturning federal hydrogen vehicle fuel safety rule
s2025-275.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 46 to overturn a 2025 federal safety rule setting fuel system and hydrogen storage tank requirements for vehicles that run on hydrogen. The resolution now goes to the House.

s2025-276.name: Taking up a resolution on California vehicle emissions waiver
s2025-276.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 46 to begin considering a resolution that would cancel the federal approval letting California enforce its Advanced Clean Cars II vehicle emission rules. This vote was only to start debate on it, not a final vote on the resolution.

s2025-277.name: Overturning California's vehicle emission rule waiver
s2025-277.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 44 to pass a joint resolution that cancels the federal approval given to California's Advanced Clean Cars II rules on vehicle pollution, which set requirements for low-emission and zero-emission vehicles.

s2025-278.name: Senate vote to take up California vehicle emissions rule repeal
s2025-278.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 46 to begin considering a resolution that would cancel an Environmental Protection Agency decision letting California enforce its own pollution standards for heavy-duty trucks and some vehicles. The vote was to start debate, not a final vote on the resolution.

s2025-279.name: Overturning California's truck emission rules
s2025-279.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 45 to pass a resolution that cancels the federal government's approval of California's rules on emissions from heavy trucks and buses, including zero-emission truck and airport shuttle requirements.

s2025-280.name: Senate vote to take up California vehicle pollution rule repeal
s2025-280.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 46 to begin considering a measure that would cancel an Environmental Protection Agency decision allowing California to set its own emissions standards for heavy-duty trucks, buses and some off-road diesel engines. Passage of the measure itself was not decided by this vote.

s2025-281.name: Disapproval of EPA rule on California vehicle pollution standards
s2025-281.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 46 to pass a resolution overturning the Environmental Protection Agency's approval of California's low-emissions standards for new heavy-duty trucks, engines and some off-road diesel equipment. The resolution cancels the agency's waiver that allowed California to enforce those standards.

s2025-305.name: Senate vote to advance the GENIUS Act on stablecoins
s2025-305.plain: The Senate voted 68 to 30 to end debate and move ahead with the GENIUS Act, which sets rules for stablecoins, digital money that must be redeemable for a fixed value. The 60 votes needed were reached. This was a step, not the final vote on the bill.

s2025-306.name: Blocking a proposed arms sale to Qatar
s2025-306.plain: The Senate voted 39 to 56 against pulling a resolution out of committee that would block a proposed sale of certain military equipment and services to Qatar. The resolution stays in committee for now.

s2025-307.name: Blocking arms sale to United Arab Emirates
s2025-307.plain: The Senate voted against moving a resolution to block a proposed military equipment sale to the United Arab Emirates out of committee, so it will not get a full Senate vote for now. The measure would have prohibited the sale of certain defense articles and services.

s2025-309.name: Motion to set aside the GENIUS Act stablecoin bill
s2025-309.plain: The Senate voted 45 to 52 on a step to set aside the GENIUS Act, which would create rules for payment stablecoins, digital assets redeemable for a fixed value. The step failed, so the bill stays under consideration.

s2025-310.name: Setting aside a Senate budget rule on a pending measure
s2025-310.plain: The Senate voted 64 to 33 to set aside a budget rule that a senator said the measure broke, so work on it could continue. The 60-vote threshold for this step was met.

s2025-311.name: Amendment to the GENIUS Act stablecoin bill
s2025-311.plain: The Senate voted 67 to 30 to adopt a proposed change that replaces the text of the GENIUS Act, a bill setting rules for stablecoins, which are digital assets meant to keep a fixed value. The bill itself was not yet passed by this vote.

s2025-312.name: Senate vote to advance the GENIUS Act on stablecoins
s2025-312.plain: The Senate voted 67 to 27 to end debate and move ahead on the GENIUS Act, which would set rules for stablecoins, digital assets meant to be redeemable for a fixed value. Because the vote needed 60 votes, it reached the required threshold.

s2025-318.name: Senate passes GENIUS Act on digital dollar rules
s2025-318.plain: The Senate voted 68 to 30 to pass the GENIUS Act, which sets rules for stablecoins, digital tokens meant to be redeemable for a fixed value, such as one U.S. dollar. Under the act, only approved issuers could offer them to U.S. users, and they would need to hold matching reserves.

s2025-328.name: Moving a bill on U.S. military action against Iran
s2025-328.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 against taking up a measure that would have required the President to end U.S. military action against Iran unless Congress had authorized it. The measure stays in committee.

s2025-329.name: Senate Votes to Begin Work on Budget Reconciliation Bill
s2025-329.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 49 to begin debate on a reconciliation bill that changes federal spending and taxes, including SNAP food assistance rules, reduces taxes, and raises the federal debt limit. This was a step to start work on the bill, not its final passage.

s2025-330.name: Senate vote on how the rules apply to a tax and spending bill
s2025-330.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 47 to uphold the presiding officer's ruling on how the Senate's rules apply to a large bill that changes taxes, federal spending, and the debt limit, with all Republicans in favor and Democrats opposed.

s2025-331.name: Senate ruling on rules for budget reconciliation bill
s2025-331.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 47 to uphold the presiding officer's ruling on how the Senate's rules apply to a large budget bill that changes taxes, spending on federal programs, and the federal debt limit. Republicans voted for the ruling and Democrats voted against it.

s2025-332.name: Senate rejects motion on budget reconciliation bill
s2025-332.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 to reject a motion on a large budget bill that changes taxes, spending on federal programs, and the government's borrowing limit. The bill itself was not voted on in this step.

s2025-333.name: Senate rejects motion on reconciliation bill
s2025-333.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 51 to reject a motion on a reconciliation bill that changes taxes, federal spending, and the debt limit, including changes to food assistance (SNAP) rules. The motion was not agreed to.

s2025-334.name: Setting aside a budget rule for a spending and tax bill
s2025-334.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 48 to set aside a Senate budget rule that a senator had said the bill breaks, so the bill could move forward. The vote needed 60 votes, three-fifths of the Senate, and 51 votes was enough to pass it. The bill reduces taxes, changes food assistance (SNAP) and other federal programs, and raises the government's borrowing limit.

s2025-335.name: Senate rejects motion on budget reconciliation bill
s2025-335.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 to reject a motion on a budget reconciliation bill that would change federal programs, including food assistance (SNAP) work requirements and benefit calculations, and raise the federal debt limit. The motion did not pass.

s2025-336.name: Senate rejects motion on budget reconciliation bill
s2025-336.plain: The Senate voted 48 to 52 to reject a motion related to a budget reconciliation bill, which would reduce taxes, change spending on various federal programs, and raise the federal debt limit. The motion did not pass.

s2025-337.name: Senate rejects motion on a budget reconciliation bill
s2025-337.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 51 to reject a motion on a large budget bill that would change taxes, spending, and the national debt limit. Because the motion was rejected, the Senate did not move forward with the bill at this step.

s2025-338.name: Senate rejects motion on budget reconciliation bill
s2025-338.plain: The Senate voted 48 to 52 to reject a motion on a large budget bill that would change taxes, spending, and the federal debt limit, along with several food assistance and other federal programs. Because the motion was rejected, the bill was not moved forward at this step.

s2025-339.name: Extending health insurance tax credits and raising top tax rate
s2025-339.plain: The Senate voted on whether to set aside a budget rule so a bill extending health insurance tax credits and raising the tax rate on incomes over $10 million could move ahead. The vote needed 60 votes and got 47 in favor, so it did not reach the 60 needed.

s2025-340.name: Motion on Budget Reconciliation Bill with Food Aid Changes
s2025-340.plain: The Senate voted on a motion about a budget reconciliation bill that reduces taxes, changes spending on federal programs, and raises the debt limit. The motion was rejected, 48 in favor to 52 against, so it did not pass.

s2025-341.name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau funding cap
s2025-341.plain: The Senate voted on whether to set aside a budget rule so a change to the consumer bureau's funding limit could move forward. The proposal needed 60 votes to do so and got 47, so it did not reach the 60 needed; the rule remains in force.

s2025-342.name: Senate vote on waiving budget rule for Medicaid funding change
s2025-342.plain: The Senate voted 56 to 44 to keep a budget rule in place, so the proposal to lower federal Medicaid funding to 80 percent for states covering certain noncitizens charged with or convicted of certain acts did not go ahead. The vote needed 60 votes to set the rule aside and fell short.

s2025-343.name: Senate vote on crypto corruption bill's budget-rule objection
s2025-343.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 on whether to set aside a budget rule so a bill to prevent cryptocurrency corruption could go ahead. The vote needed 60 votes to succeed and did not reach that number, so the rule stayed in force and the bill did not move forward.

s2025-344.name: Vote to set aside Senate budget rule
s2025-344.plain: The Senate voted on whether to set aside a Senate budget rule so a measure could move ahead. The vote needed 60 votes to succeed and got 49 in favor and 51 against, so it did not reach the 60 needed and the rule stays in force.

s2025-345.name: Medicaid and CHIP coverage limited to verified citizens
s2025-345.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 47 on whether to set aside a budget rule so a bill could move ahead. The bill would bar federal Medicaid and CHIP funding for people without verified citizenship or satisfactory immigration status. Because 60 votes were needed and only 53 were cast in favor, the request did not reach the 60 votes required, so the rule stayed in force.

s2025-346.name: Motion on Budget Reconciliation Bill With Spending and Tax Changes
s2025-346.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 to reject a motion on a budget reconciliation bill that cuts taxes, changes spending on federal programs, and raises the government's borrowing limit. The motion did not pass.

s2025-347.name: Motion on budget reconciliation bill with SNAP changes
s2025-347.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 to reject a motion on a budget reconciliation bill that reduces taxes, changes spending on federal programs, and raises the debt limit. The bill includes changes to the food assistance program SNAP, such as expanded work requirements for some recipients.

s2025-348.name: Senate rejects motion on budget reconciliation bill
s2025-348.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 to reject a motion on a large budget bill that changes taxes, spending, and the federal debt limit, along with many federal programs such as food assistance. The motion did not pass, so the bill was not advanced by this vote.

s2025-349.name: Senate rejects motion on budget reconciliation bill
s2025-349.plain: The Senate voted on a motion about a budget reconciliation bill that would change several federal programs, including food assistance (SNAP) work rules and benefit calculations. The motion was rejected, 48 in favor and 52 against.

s2025-350.name: Motion on a budget reconciliation bill with SNAP and tax changes
s2025-350.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 51 to reject a motion on a large budget bill that changes food assistance and taxes, along with other federal programs. Because the motion was rejected, this step did not advance the bill.

s2025-351.name: Senate rejects motion on budget reconciliation bill
s2025-351.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 to reject a motion on a budget reconciliation bill that would change taxes, spending and the debt limit, including changes to SNAP food assistance work requirements and benefit calculations. The motion did not pass.

s2025-352.name: Limiting use of Defense Production Act funds without Congress
s2025-352.plain: The Senate voted on whether to set aside a budget rule so a measure could move forward, which needed 60 votes. The vote was 42 in favor and 58 against, so it did not reach the 60 votes needed. The measure would bar using Defense Production Act funds without congressional approval.

s2025-353.name: Senate rejects motion on budget reconciliation bill
s2025-353.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 to reject a motion on a budget reconciliation bill that changes taxes, spending, and the federal debt limit, including changes to SNAP food assistance work requirements and benefit calculations. The motion did not pass.

s2025-354.name: Senate rejects motion on budget reconciliation bill
s2025-354.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 to reject a motion on a budget reconciliation bill that would change taxes, spending and the debt limit, including changes to the food assistance program SNAP. The motion was not agreed to.

s2025-355.name: Vote on waiving budget rules for tax and rural health bill
s2025-355.plain: The Senate voted on whether to set aside a budget rule so a bill could go ahead. The measure would apply a 39.6 percent individual income tax rate and provide added funding for rural health programs. The vote needed 60 votes to pass and got 22, so it did not reach the 60 needed.

s2025-356.name: Tax deduction for home educators: budget rule waiver
s2025-356.plain: The Senate voted 54 to 46 on whether to set aside a budget rule so a bill giving home educators a tax deduction could go ahead. The vote fell short of the 60 votes needed, so the rule stayed in place.

s2025-357.name: Senate rejects motion on budget reconciliation bill
s2025-357.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 to reject a motion on a budget reconciliation bill that would change taxes, spending and the debt limit, including changes to food assistance (SNAP) work requirements and benefit calculations. The motion did not pass.

s2025-358.name: Amendment to end school scholarship program rejected
s2025-358.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 50 on a proposed change to a large budget bill that would have eliminated a program of scholarships for elementary and secondary education at public, private, or religious schools. The change was rejected, so the scholarship program stays in the bill.

s2025-359.name: Senate rejects motion on a budget reconciliation bill
s2025-359.plain: The Senate voted 48 to 51 to reject a motion on a reconciliation bill that changes taxes, spending on federal programs, and the federal debt limit. The bill would also change SNAP food assistance rules, including work requirements and how benefits are calculated. The motion itself was not a final vote on the bill.

s2025-360.name: Amendment to end wind and solar tax credits
s2025-360.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the bill that would have ended tax credits for wind and solar energy, by a vote of 21 in favor to 79 against.

s2025-361.name: Amendment to remove Medicaid payment limits from reconciliation bill
s2025-361.plain: The Senate voted 48 to 52 against a proposed change that would have removed a provision limiting certain Medicaid payments from the larger bill, so the change was rejected.

s2025-362.name: Amendment to cut Medicare drug prices and add dental, vision, hearing
s2025-362.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the bill that would have cut prescription drug prices under Medicare in half and added dental, vision, and hearing coverage to Medicare. The vote was 47 in favor and 53 against, short of the 60 votes needed.

s2025-363.name: Removing AI support section from tax and spending bill
s2025-363.plain: The Senate voted 99 to 1 to approve a change that removes a section of the bill providing support for artificial intelligence. The change takes that section out of the bill.

s2025-364.name: Amendment on tax parity for wind and solar facilities
s2025-364.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 to reject a proposed change to the bill that would have maintained equal tax treatment for wind and solar energy facilities under the federal tax code. The change was not adopted.

s2025-365.name: Amendment on ending the home clean energy tax credit
s2025-365.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 48 to reject a proposed change to the bill that would have altered when the residential clean energy tax credit ends. The change was not adopted.

s2025-366.name: Amendment to keep clean energy tax credits rejected
s2025-366.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 51 to reject a proposed change that would have repealed the changes ending certain clean energy tax credits in the larger spending and tax bill. The change was not adopted.

s2025-367.name: Using airport lease money for aviation safety
s2025-367.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the bill that would have used lease payments from Washington-area airports for aviation safety improvements and other purposes. The vote was 50 in favor and 50 against.

s2025-368.name: Amendment to remove funding for the Office of Management and Budget
s2025-368.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 50 on a proposed change to the bill that would have removed funding for the Office of Management and Budget. The change was rejected, so the funding stays in the bill.

s2025-369.name: Amendment to delay SNAP matching funds rule rejected
s2025-369.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change that would have removed a provision delaying when states must meet new matching-funds requirements for the food assistance program known as SNAP. The vote was 45 in favor and 55 against.

s2025-370.name: Amendment to the tax and spending bill
s2025-370.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 50, and the Vice President broke the tie to adopt a proposed change to the bill. The facts do not state what the change itself would do.

s2025-371.name: Substitute version of the tax and spending bill adopted
s2025-371.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 50, and the Vice President broke the tie in favor, adopting a replacement version of the bill that reduces taxes, changes spending on many federal programs, and raises the federal debt limit.

s2025-372.name: Senate passes major tax and spending reconciliation bill
s2025-372.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 50, and the Vice President broke the tie in favor, passing the bill. It reduces taxes, changes some federal spending programs including food assistance for some adults, and raises the federal debt limit.

s2025-391.name: Senate vote to move the Rescissions Act of 2025 to the floor
s2025-391.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 50, with the Vice President casting the tie-breaking vote, to take the Rescissions Act of 2025 out of committee so the full Senate can consider it. The act would cancel certain unspent funds for foreign aid, international organizations, and public broadcasting.

s2025-392.name: Senate vote to begin work on rescissions bill
s2025-392.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 50, with the Vice President breaking the tie in favor, to start debate on the Rescissions Act of 2025. The act would cancel certain unspent funds for foreign aid, the U.S. Agency for International Development, several independent agencies, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

s2025-393.name: Amendment to restore international disaster aid funds
s2025-393.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the Rescissions Act of 2025 that would have removed the cancellation of unspent international disaster assistance funds. The vote was 49 in favor and 50 against.

s2025-394.name: Motion on the Rescissions Act of 2025
s2025-394.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 48 to reject a motion to send the Rescissions Act of 2025 back for changes. The act would cancel certain unspent funds for foreign aid, international programs, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

s2025-395.name: Motion on Rescissions Act of 2025 Rejected
s2025-395.plain: The Senate voted 48 to 51 to reject a motion sent back to committee on the Rescissions Act of 2025, which would cancel certain unspent funds for foreign aid, international organizations, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting. The rejection means the motion did not pass, and the bill continued without that change.

s2025-396.name: Motion on the Rescissions Act of 2025
s2025-396.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 48 to reject a motion to send the Rescissions Act of 2025 back for further changes. The act would cancel certain unspent funds for foreign aid, international programs, and public broadcasting.

s2025-397.name: Restoring Public Broadcasting Funding Amendment
s2025-397.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change that would have removed the Corporation for Public Broadcasting from the bill's cuts, so its funding would have stayed in place. The vote was 47 in favor and 52 against.

s2025-398.name: Motion on the Rescissions Act of 2025
s2025-398.plain: The Senate rejected a motion, 48 to 51, that would have sent the Rescissions Act of 2025 back for further consideration. The act would cancel certain unspent funds for foreign aid, international organizations, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

s2025-399.name: Motion on the Rescissions Act of 2025
s2025-399.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 47 to reject a motion to send the Rescissions Act of 2025 back to committee. The act would cancel certain unspent funds for foreign aid, certain independent agencies, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

s2025-400.name: Amendment to keep more global health funding
s2025-400.plain: The Senate voted against a proposed change to the Rescissions Act of 2025 that would have reduced the amount of money cut from global health programs, in order to keep funding for disease programs. The vote was 46 in favor and 51 against, so the change was rejected.

s2025-401.name: Motion on the Rescissions Act of 2025
s2025-401.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 47 to reject a motion to send the Rescissions Act of 2025 back to committee. The act would cancel certain unspent foreign aid and public broadcasting funds.

s2025-402.name: Amendment to keep global health funding
s2025-402.plain: The Senate voted 48 to 51 to reject a proposed change to the Rescissions Act of 2025. The change would have removed the cancellation of funds for global health programs, including family planning and reproductive health.

s2025-403.name: Motion on the Rescissions Act of 2025
s2025-403.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 48 to reject a motion to send the Rescissions Act of 2025 back to committee. The act would cancel certain unspent funds for foreign aid, international organizations, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

s2025-404.name: Amendment to keep Feed the Future funding
s2025-404.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the Rescissions Act of 2025 that would have kept funds for the Feed the Future program, which aims to improve global food security and agricultural resilience. The vote was 48 in favor and 51 against.

s2025-405.name: Senate sets aside amendment on foreign aid cuts
s2025-405.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 47 to set aside a proposed change to the Rescissions Act of 2025, which would cancel certain unspent funds for foreign aid, international programs, and public broadcasting. Setting it aside ends it without a direct vote on the change.

s2025-406.name: Proposed changes to the Rescissions Act of 2025
s2025-406.plain: The Senate voted down a proposed change to the Rescissions Act of 2025, 51 to 47. The bill would cancel unspent federal funds for foreign aid, certain international programs, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting. The rejected change would have altered that bill.

s2025-407.name: Reducing cuts to Europe and Central Asia aid in rescissions bill
s2025-407.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 49 to reject a change that would have reduced the amount of money cut from aid for Europe, Eurasia, and Central Asia in the Rescissions Act of 2025.

s2025-408.name: Amendment to restore UNICEF and reduce rescinded aid
s2025-408.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the Rescissions Act of 2025 that would have reduced the aid taken back from international organizations and programs and made sure UNICEF receives all the funding Congress previously provided. The vote was 48 in favor and 51 against.

s2025-409.name: Keeping $15 million for the U.S. Institute of Peace
s2025-409.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 48 against a proposed change that would have removed the $15 million cut to the U.S. Institute of Peace from the bill. The change was rejected, so the cut stays in the bill.

s2025-410.name: Substitute version of the Rescissions Act of 2025
s2025-410.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 47 to adopt a replacement version of the Rescissions Act of 2025. The act would cancel specified unspent funds previously provided to the State Department, USAID, several independent agencies, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

s2025-411.name: Rescissions Act of 2025 final passage vote
s2025-411.plain: The Senate passed the Rescissions Act of 2025, 51 to 48. The measure cancels specified unspent funds for foreign aid, certain U.S. agencies, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, with some programs exempted.

s2025-422.name: Senate Votes to Begin Work on 2026 Spending Bills
s2025-422.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 48 to start working on a package of three 2026 federal spending bills covering military construction, veterans affairs, agriculture and the legislative branch. This vote only opened debate; it did not pass the bills themselves.

s2025-423.name: Senate Moves Ahead on Three Funding Bills for 2026
s2025-423.plain: The Senate voted 91 to 7 to end debate and move ahead on a bill that would provide 2026 funding for military construction, veterans programs, agriculture, and the Senate itself. The vote cleared the 60 votes needed.

s2025-428.name: Senate Votes to Begin Work on Three Spending Bills
s2025-428.plain: The Senate voted 90 to 8 to begin debate on a bill that provides money for fiscal year 2026 to military construction and veterans programs, agriculture and food agencies, and the legislative branch. The vote was a step to start work on the bill, not its final passage.

s2025-454.name: Blocking a vote on arms sales to Israel
s2025-454.plain: The Senate voted 70 to 27 to keep a resolution opposing a proposed export of certain firearms, parts and components to Israel in committee, rather than bringing it to the full Senate. The resolution would have prohibited that export.

s2025-455.name: Blocking arms sale to Israel: Senate motion fails
s2025-455.plain: The Senate voted 24 to 73 against moving a resolution to block a proposed weapons and defense sale to Israel out of committee for full Senate consideration. The resolution would have prohibited that sale.

s2025-472.name: Limiting rescissions of federal funding
s2025-472.plain: The Senate voted on whether to set aside a budget rule so a measure limiting cancellations of federal funding could go ahead. The proposal needed 60 votes to set the rule aside and got 44 votes in favor, so it did not reach the 60 needed.

s2025-473.name: Report on veterans who die by suicide with firearms
s2025-473.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the 2026 spending bill for military construction, veterans, agriculture and Congress that would have required a report on veterans who would have been flagged in the national instant background check system and who die by suicide with a firearm. The vote was 44 in favor and 51 against.

s2025-474.name: Blocking Agriculture Department reorganization funding
s2025-474.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to a spending bill for military construction, veterans, agriculture and Congress. The change would have barred money from being used to reorganize the Agriculture Department and required a cost-benefit analysis, a public comment period and a report first. The vote was 42 in favor and 53 against.

s2025-475.name: Report on VA workforce reduction plan for 2026
s2025-475.plain: The Senate voted 45 to 50 against a proposed change to the spending bill that would have required the Veterans Affairs Secretary to report to Congress on the department's plan to reduce its workforce in 2026. The change was rejected.

s2025-476.name: Cutting Agriculture funding by 2 percent across the board
s2025-476.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change that would have cut the bill's Agriculture funding by 2 percent across the board, with 14 in favor and 81 against.

s2025-477.name: Cutting farm and food agency funding
s2025-477.plain: The Senate rejected a proposal to reduce funding for certain programs in the agriculture, rural development, and food and drug agency part of the spending bill, by a vote of 15 to 81.

s2025-478.name: Amendment on disclosing earmarks in spending bill
s2025-478.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the 2026 spending bill for military construction, veterans, agriculture and Congress, by 21 votes in favor to 75 against. The change would have limited disclosures about earmarks, which are funds directed to specific projects.

s2025-480.name: Funding for military construction, veterans, agriculture and Congress
s2025-480.plain: The Senate approved a bill providing money for military construction, veterans' programs, agriculture and food safety, and the legislative branch, by 87 votes to 9. The measure was a final vote on the bill itself.

s2025-481.name: Change to 2026 military, veterans, agriculture and Senate funding bill
s2025-481.plain: The Senate voted 81 to 15 to approve a proposed change to a bill that provides 2026 funding for military construction, veterans programs, agriculture and the Food and Drug Administration, and the Senate. The specific change is not described in the official facts.

s2025-500.name: Senate vote to advance the 2026 defense authorization bill
s2025-500.plain: The Senate voted 84 to 14 to end debate and move ahead on the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, which sets policies and authorities for Defense Department programs and military construction. The vote cleared the 60 votes needed, but it was a step toward taking up the bill, not a vote on final passage.

s2025-503.name: Senate Opens Debate on 2026 Defense Bill
s2025-503.plain: The Senate voted 83 to 13 to begin working on the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, which sets policies for military programs, equipment purchases, and personnel levels for 2026. The bill does not itself provide the money; that comes from separate spending legislation.

s2025-510.name: Senate sets aside resolution on confirming several nominees
s2025-510.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 46 to set aside a resolution that would have allowed it to confirm a group of nominees for executive posts and ambassadorships, including to Argentina, Greece, Liechtenstein and Sweden. Setting it aside ends the resolution without a direct vote on it.

s2025-511.name: Senate Votes to Begin Work on Batch of Nominations
s2025-511.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 45 to begin considering a group of government nominees at once, including officials for the Defense, Energy, Interior and Labor departments and ambassadors to Argentina, Greece, Liechtenstein and Sweden. This was a step to start the work, not the final confirmation vote.

s2025-512.name: Motion to set aside the 2026 defense policy bill
s2025-512.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 49 to set aside a motion related to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, a bill that sets policies and authorizations for Department of Defense programs, military construction, and certain Department of Energy national security programs. Setting it aside usually ends that motion.

s2025-513.name: Senate vote on grouping nominations for confirmation
s2025-513.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 47 on whether to end debate on a resolution that would let senators consider several nominations together, including executive officers for the Defense, Energy, Interior and Labor departments and ambassadors to Argentina, Greece, Liechtenstein and Sweden. The vote needed 60 votes to end debate and fell short, so the step did not go forward.

s2025-514.name: Senate vote to reconsider a group of nominations
s2025-514.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 45 to agree to reconsider an earlier decision about confirming a group of nominees for government and ambassador posts. The nominees would serve in the Defense, Energy, Interior, and Labor departments and as ambassadors to Argentina, Greece, Liechtenstein, and Sweden.

s2025-515.name: Senate ruling on confirming groups of nominees
s2025-515.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 45 not to uphold the presiding officer's ruling on how the Senate's rules apply to confirming a group of nominees at once. The nominees would serve in the Defense, Energy, Interior and Labor departments and as ambassadors to Argentina, Greece, Liechtenstein and Sweden.

s2025-516.name: Vote to advance a package of executive nominations
s2025-516.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 43 to end debate and move ahead on a resolution that would allow a group of nominees for executive posts and ambassadorships to be considered together. The nominees would serve in the Defense, Energy, Interior, and Labor departments and as ambassadors to Argentina, Greece, Liechtenstein, and Sweden.

s2025-517.name: Senate approves batch of executive and ambassador nominations
s2025-517.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 44 to approve a single resolution that allows a group of nominees for executive posts in the Defense, Energy, Interior and Labor departments, and ambassadors to Argentina, Greece, Liechtenstein and Sweden, to be considered together.

s2025-520.name: Senate vote on Indiana power plant pollution rule
s2025-520.plain: The Senate voted against starting work on a measure that would cancel an Environmental Protection Agency rule. The rule lets Indiana power plants release more nitrogen oxide pollution from May through September. The vote was 47 in favor and 51 against.

s2025-521.name: Senate Rejects Starting Work on Federal Budget Plan
s2025-521.plain: The Senate voted 36 to 62 not to begin work on a budget resolution setting federal spending and revenue targets for 2026 and later years. Republicans mostly voted yes and Democrats all voted no. The vote did not begin debate on the budget plan.

s2025-523.name: Senate vote to reconsider a batch of executive nominations
s2025-523.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 47 to agree to a motion to reconsider an earlier action on a large group of executive-branch nominations, including ambassadors and agency officials. The vote was along party lines, with all Republicans in favor and all Democrats opposed.

s2025-524.name: Senate vote on rules for nominations package
s2025-524.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 52 against upholding the presiding officer's ruling on how the Senate's rules apply to a package of government nominations. The ruling was not upheld, so the ruling does not stand.

s2025-527.name: Stopgap Government Funding Bill Fails in Senate
s2025-527.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 45 on the stopgap bill to keep federal agencies funded past October 1, 2025. It did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the bill was not passed. The bill would have kept most programs at last year's funding levels and extended the expanded health insurance premium tax credit.

s2025-528.name: Bill to end government shutdown fails in Senate
s2025-528.plain: The Senate voted 44 to 48 on a measure to end the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025, funding most federal agencies through January 30, 2026. The measure did not reach the 60 votes needed, so it was not approved.

s2025-533.name: Senate vote to advance bill preventing government shutdowns
s2025-533.plain: The Senate voted 37 to 61 on whether to end debate and move ahead on the Eliminate Shutdowns Act. The vote needed 60 votes to succeed and did not reach that number, so the bill is blocked for now. The bill would keep government programs funded at last year's rate if full funding bills are not passed before the fiscal year begins.

s2025-534.name: Stopgap government funding bill with health tax credit extension
s2025-534.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 on whether to pass a bill to keep federal agencies funded past October 1, 2025, and extend the expanded tax credit for health insurance premiums. It did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the bill was not approved.

s2025-535.name: Bill to end government shutdown and fund agencies
s2025-535.plain: The Senate voted 55 to 45 on the final bill to end the government shutdown and temporarily fund most federal agencies through January 30, 2026. The measure did not reach the 60 votes needed, so it was not passed.

s2025-536.name: Ending debate on a federal funding bill
s2025-536.plain: The Senate voted on whether to end debate and move ahead on a bill that would keep federal agencies funded past October 1 and extend expanded health insurance tax credits. The vote fell short, with 47 for and 53 against, so it did not reach the 60 votes needed, and the bill cannot move forward for now.

s2025-537.name: Ending debate on a 2026 government funding bill
s2025-537.plain: The Senate voted on whether to end debate and move ahead on a bill to keep federal agencies funded and end the government shutdown. The vote was 55 to 45, short of the 60 votes needed, so the Senate did not move ahead on it.

s2025-540.name: Senate vote to advance a package of nominations
s2025-540.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 46 to end debate and move ahead on a resolution that would allow a group of presidential nominees on the Executive Calendar to be considered together. All Republicans voting supported it, and Democrats voting opposed it.

s2025-541.name: Resolution to group and confirm certain nominations together
s2025-541.plain: The Senate approved a resolution allowing a batch of nominations on the Executive Calendar to be considered together, 51 to 46. Republicans voted yes and Democrats voted no.

s2025-542.name: Vote to advance the government funding and extensions bill fails
s2025-542.plain: The Senate voted on whether to end debate and move ahead on a bill to keep federal funding going and extend several programs, including expanded health insurance tax credits. The vote was 46 for and 52 against, short of the 60 votes needed, so the Senate did not move ahead for now.

s2025-543.name: Ending the 2025 government shutdown: vote to begin work on funding bill
s2025-543.plain: The Senate voted on whether to end debate and begin work on a bill that would fund most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, and end the government shutdown. The vote needed 60 votes to succeed and fell short, with 54 in favor and 44 against, so the Senate did not move ahead on the bill.

s2025-544.name: Senate vote to end debate on spending and health care bill
s2025-544.plain: The Senate voted 45 to 50 on whether to end debate and move ahead on a bill to keep federal agencies funded past October 1, 2025, and to extend expanded health insurance tax credits. The vote did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the bill is blocked for now.

s2025-545.name: Vote to end debate on shutdown-ending funding bill
s2025-545.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 42 to end debate and move ahead on a bill to end the government shutdown and fund most federal agencies through January 30, 2026. The vote did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the bill is blocked for now.

s2025-548.name: Opening Montana federal land in Miles City area to coal leasing
s2025-548.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 47 to begin debate on a measure to cancel a Bureau of Land Management plan that had made no land in the Miles City area in eastern Montana available for coal leasing. The vote was to start work on the measure, not a final vote on it.

s2025-549.name: Opening Montana federal land to coal leasing
s2025-549.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 47 to pass a resolution overturning a Bureau of Land Management plan that had made no acres available for coal leasing in eastern Montana. Passing it removes that plan, which would open the land to coal leasing.

s2025-550.name: Vote to end debate on a government funding bill
s2025-550.plain: The Senate did not end debate on a bill to keep federal agencies funded past October 1 and extend expiring programs, so it did not reach the 60 votes needed to move ahead. The vote was 47 in favor and 52 against.

s2025-551.name: Ending Debate on Shutdown-Ending Funding Bill
s2025-551.plain: The Senate voted 54 to 45 to end debate and move ahead on a bill to fund most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, ending the government shutdown. The vote did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the Senate did not move ahead on it.

s2025-553.name: Senate takes up North Dakota land management plan rollback
s2025-553.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 47 to begin considering a resolution that would overturn a federal land management plan for North Dakota, issued in January 2025. The plan limited oil and gas development in some low-potential areas and limited new coal leasing to areas within four miles of existing mines.

s2025-554.name: Ending the national energy emergency declaration
s2025-554.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 51 against a measure that would have ended the national emergency declared on energy policy by the President in January 2025. The measure did not pass.

s2025-555.name: Bill to end unauthorized military hostilities
s2025-555.plain: The Senate voted 48 to 51 against moving a resolution out of committee, so it stays in committee. The resolution would direct removal of U.S. armed forces from hostilities Congress has not authorized.

s2025-556.name: Overturning Dakota land management plan for oil and coal
s2025-556.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 45 to pass a resolution that cancels a Bureau of Land Management plan for North Dakota public lands. The plan had limited oil and gas development in low-potential areas and limited new coal leasing to areas within four miles of existing mines.

s2025-557.name: Vote to end debate on government funding bill
s2025-557.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 50 to end debate and move ahead on a bill to keep federal agencies funded past October 1, 2025, and extend some expiring programs. It did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the bill is blocked for now.

s2025-558.name: Vote to end debate on government funding bill
s2025-558.plain: The Senate did not reach the 60 votes needed to end debate and move ahead on a bill to keep the federal government funded through January 30, 2026, and to end the shutdown that began October 1, 2025. The vote was 54 in favor and 45 against.

s2025-559.name: Senate vote to take up Central Yukon land plan rule
s2025-559.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 47 to begin considering a resolution that would cancel a Bureau of Land Management rule on the Central Yukon land management plan in Alaska. The resolution would nullify the rule, which set aside about 3.6 million acres as areas of critical environmental concern or research natural areas.

s2025-560.name: Resolution to overturn Central Yukon land management plan
s2025-560.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 46 to pass a resolution that cancels a Bureau of Land Management rule adopting a new land management plan for Alaska's Central Yukon area, which had set aside about 3.6 million acres for environmental protection or research.

s2025-562.name: Proposed change to defense bill on Federal Reserve bank earnings
s2025-562.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the defense authorization bill that would have banned earnings on balances that banks keep at the Federal Reserve. The change needed 60 votes to pass and got 14, so it did not reach that threshold.

s2025-563.name: Senate confirmation for Federal Reserve and consumer bureau watchdogs
s2025-563.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the defense bill that would have required the President to nominate, and the Senate to confirm, the inspectors general overseeing the Federal Reserve Board and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. The vote was 53 in favor and 43 against, which was short of the 60 votes needed.

s2025-564.name: Changing military and federal pay adjustments for certain locations
s2025-564.plain: The Senate did not approve a proposed change to the defense bill that would have required a review of how locality pay amounts are set and a pilot program testing other methods. The vote was 51 in favor and 46 against, but the change needed 60 votes to be adopted, so it was rejected.

s2025-565.name: Amendment to bar foreign aircraft for presidential airlift
s2025-565.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the defense bill that would have barred spending money to buy or modify foreign aircraft for presidential travel. The vote was 46 in favor and 50 against, and the change needed 60 votes to be adopted, so it did not reach that number.

s2025-566.name: Limits on National Guard full-time duty in states
s2025-566.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the defense bill that would have clarified limits on full-time National Guard duty performed in a state, territory, or the District of Columbia. The change needed 60 votes to be adopted and got 47.

s2025-567.name: Amendment limiting military support for civilian police rejected
s2025-567.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the defense bill that would have limited how much the armed forces can help civilian law enforcement. The vote was 46 in favor and 52 against, and 60 votes were needed for the change to pass.

s2025-568.name: Proposed cut to defense budget for veteran dental care
s2025-568.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the defense bill that would have cut the Pentagon budget by 10 percent and expanded veteran dental care at the Department of Veterans Affairs. The change needed 60 votes to pass and got 10 yes votes, with 88 voting no.

s2025-569.name: Limiting federal officers' use in crowd control
s2025-569.plain: The Senate rejected a proposed change to the defense bill that would have limited the use of federal law enforcement officers for crowd control. The vote was 47 in favor and 50 against, short of the 60 votes needed for the change to be adopted.

s2025-570.name: Final Senate vote on 2026 defense authorization bill
s2025-570.plain: The Senate voted 77 to 20 to pass the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, which sets policies and authorizes funding levels for military programs, equipment, personnel and construction. The bill itself does not provide the actual money, which comes through separate spending legislation.

s2025-571.name: Vote to end debate on government funding bill
s2025-571.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 45 to end debate so it could start work on a bill that would fund most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, and end the government shutdown. The vote fell short of the 60 votes needed, so the Senate did not move ahead with the bill.

s2025-572.name: Vote to end debate on government funding bill
s2025-572.plain: The Senate voted on whether to end debate so it could begin work on a bill to keep most federal agencies funded through January 30, 2026, and end the government shutdown. The vote was 51 in favor and 44 against, which fell short of the 60 votes needed, so the Senate did not move ahead on it.

s2025-573.name: Vote to end debate on a government funding bill
s2025-573.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 45 to end debate so it could start work on a bill to keep federal agencies funded through January 30, 2026, and end the government shutdown. This did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the Senate did not move ahead on the bill.

s2025-575.name: Vote to advance the 2026 defense spending bill
s2025-575.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 44 to end debate and begin work on the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026, which funds military activities. The vote did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the bill remains blocked for now.

s2025-576.name: Ending the 2025 shutdown: Senate vote to advance funding bill
s2025-576.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 43 to end debate and move ahead on a bill to fund most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, ending the shutdown that began October 1, 2025. The vote fell short of the 60 votes needed, so the bill was not advanced.

s2025-581.name: Vote to end debate on shutdown-ending funding bill
s2025-581.plain: The Senate voted 54 to 46 to end debate on a bill that would end the government shutdown and keep most federal agencies funded through January 30, 2026. The vote did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the Senate did not move ahead on the bill.

s2025-585.name: Paying federal workers during government shutdowns
s2025-585.plain: The Senate voted to end debate on the Shutdown Fairness Act so it could move ahead, but the vote fell short of the 60 votes needed, with 54 in favor and 45 against. The bill would provide money to pay federal employees who must work during a government shutdown.

s2025-590.name: Ending the 2025 government shutdown: Senate debate vote
s2025-590.plain: The Senate voted 54 to 45 to end debate on a bill to fund most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, which would end the government shutdown. The vote needed 60 votes to succeed, so it did not reach the 60 votes needed and the bill stays blocked for now.

s2025-594.name: Ending the emergency behind tariffs on Brazilian imports
s2025-594.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 48 to end the national emergency that President Trump declared in July 2025 to justify an extra 40% tariff on certain Brazilian imports. The order's exemptions, such as civil aircraft, wood pulp, precious metals, energy and fertilizers, would still apply.

s2025-595.name: Senate votes to begin work on Alaska oil reserve land rule
s2025-595.plain: The Senate voted 54 to 46 to start work on a measure that would undo a 2022 plan limiting oil and gas leasing in part of Alaska's National Petroleum Reserve, reopening roughly half that land to leasing.

s2025-597.name: Senate Declines to Take Up Barred Owl Management Rule Repeal
s2025-597.plain: The Senate voted 72 to 25 not to begin considering a resolution that would overturn a Fish and Wildlife Service rule on managing barred owls in Washington, Oregon, and California. The resolution itself was not voted on.

s2025-598.name: Ending the emergency tariffs on Canadian imports
s2025-598.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 46 to pass a measure ending the national emergency the president declared to impose an additional 25% tariff on most imports from Canada. Canadian energy products face a separate 10% additional tariff under the same emergency.

s2025-599.name: Reopening oil and gas leasing in Alaska's National Petroleum Reserve
s2025-599.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 45 to pass a measure that cancels a 2022 federal plan closing about 48% of the Alaska reserve to oil and gas leasing, restoring the 2020 plan's terms.

s2025-600.name: Ending the emergency behind global tariffs
s2025-600.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 47 to pass a measure ending the national emergency President Trump declared in April 2025 that imposed a 10% tariff on most imports to the United States and extra duties on certain trading partners. Four Republicans joined all Democrats in voting yes.

s2025-603.name: Ending Debate on Funding Bill to Reopen Government
s2025-603.plain: The Senate voted 54 to 44 to end debate on a bill to fund most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, ending a government shutdown. The 60 votes needed were not reached, so the Senate did not move ahead on the bill.

s2025-608.name: Senate vote on ending military action against Venezuela
s2025-608.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 51 against moving a measure out of committee for full Senate consideration. The measure would have directed the President to end U.S. military hostilities within or against Venezuela unless Congress had declared war or authorized the force, while allowing the U.S. to defend itself against an attack.

s2025-609.name: Paying federal workers during a government shutdown
s2025-609.plain: The Senate voted 53 to 43 to end debate on the Shutdown Fairness Act, which would pay federal workers required to work during a government shutdown. The measure did not reach the 60 votes needed, so it remains blocked for now.

s2025-610.name: Vote to end debate on shutdown-ending funding bill
s2025-610.plain: The Senate voted 60 to 40 to end debate and move ahead on a bill that ends the government shutdown by funding most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, with some agencies funded through the end of 2026. The vote reached the 60 votes needed.

s2025-611.name: Senate Votes to Begin Work on Government Funding Bill
s2025-611.plain: The Senate voted 60 to 40 to begin considering a bill that would end the government shutdown that started October 1, 2025, by funding most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, and funding agriculture, military construction and veterans affairs, and legislative branch programs through the end of fiscal 2026.

s2025-612.name: Motion to set aside the government funding bill
s2025-612.plain: The Senate voted on whether to set aside the bill that ends the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025, and keeps most federal agencies funded through January 30, 2026. The motion failed, 47 in favor to 53 against, so the bill stays alive.

s2025-613.name: Motion to set aside the shutdown-ending funding bill
s2025-613.plain: The Senate voted 47 to 53 on a request to set aside the bill that would end the government shutdown and fund most federal agencies through January 30, 2026. The request failed, so the bill stays under consideration.

s2025-614.name: Motion to set aside an amendment on the funding bill
s2025-614.plain: The Senate voted 76 to 24 to set aside a proposed change to the bill that ends the government shutdown and funds most federal agencies through January 30, 2026. Setting it aside means the change will not get a direct vote.

s2025-615.name: Ending the government shutdown: funding bill advances
s2025-615.plain: The Senate voted 60 to 40 to end debate and move ahead on a bill that would fund most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, ending the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025. The 60 votes needed were reached.

s2025-616.name: Replacing the text of the funding bill to end the shutdown
s2025-616.plain: The Senate voted 60 to 40 to replace the bill's text with a substitute version. The substitute, called the Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026, would end the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025, by funding most federal agencies through January 30, 2026.

s2025-617.name: Ending the 2025 government shutdown and funding federal agencies
s2025-617.plain: The Senate voted 60 to 40 to end debate and move ahead on a measure that would end the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025, by continuing funding for most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, and funding agriculture, military construction and veterans affairs, and legislative branch programs through the end of the fiscal year. The 60 votes needed were reached.

s2025-618.name: Ending the government shutdown and funding federal agencies through January 30, 2026
s2025-618.plain: The Senate passed a bill to end the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025, by continuing funding for most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, and funding agriculture, military construction and veterans affairs, and legislative branch programs through the end of fiscal year 2026. The vote was 60 yes, 40 no.

s2025-621.name: Senate Vote to Take Up Buffalo, Wyoming Coal Leasing Rule Dispute
s2025-621.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 47 to begin considering a resolution that would overturn a Bureau of Land Management change ending future federal coal leasing in the Buffalo Field Office area of Wyoming. The resolution would require the agency to restore the 2015 plan, which made coal available for leasing.

s2025-622.name: Senate Vote to Take Up Oil and Gas Methane Rule Repeal
s2025-622.plain: The Senate voted 46 to 51 not to begin work on a measure that would cancel an Environmental Protection Agency change extending deadlines for oil and natural gas pollution rules. The change would restore the earlier deadlines, so the measure did not advance.

s2025-623.name: Overturning Wyoming coal leasing restrictions rule
s2025-623.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 43 to pass a resolution that cancels a Bureau of Land Management rule. The rule had made federal coal in the Buffalo Field Office area in Wyoming unavailable for future leasing. The resolution requires the agency to return to the earlier management plan, which allows coal leasing there.

s2025-630.name: Senate Votes to Take Up Arctic Refuge Oil Drilling Rule Dispute
s2025-630.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 47 to begin work on a resolution that would cancel a 2024 Interior Department rule limiting oil and gas leasing in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge's Coastal Plain. The vote was to start debate, not a final decision on the resolution.

s2025-632.name: Opening Arctic wildlife refuge land to oil and gas leasing
s2025-632.plain: The Senate voted 49 to 45 to pass a resolution that cancels a December 2024 federal decision limiting oil and gas leasing in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. The cancellation would restore the earlier plan making the roughly 1.6 million-acre coastal plain area available for leasing.

s2025-633.name: Senate vote to advance a package of nominations
s2025-633.plain: The Senate voted 43 to 37 to end debate on a resolution that would allow a group of presidential nominees on the calendar to be considered together. The vote needed 60 votes to succeed, so it was not approved and debate continues for now.

s2025-641.name: Senate vote to take up HHS rule disapproval resolution
s2025-641.plain: The Senate voted 50 to 49 to begin debate on a resolution that would overturn a Health and Human Services rule about how it applies the Administrative Procedure Act. The vote was a step to start work on the measure, not a final vote on it.

s2025-642.name: Senate Moves Ahead on Group Confirmation of Nominees
s2025-642.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 47 to end debate and move ahead on a measure allowing several nominees on the Executive Calendar to be considered and confirmed together as a group. Republicans voted yes and Democrats voted no.

s2025-643.name: Senate vote on Health Care Freedom for Patients Act
s2025-643.plain: The Senate voted on whether to end debate and move ahead on the Health Care Freedom for Patients Act. The vote was 51 in favor and 48 against, which did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the bill remains blocked for now. The measure would deposit federal payments into health savings accounts for some people with bronze or catastrophic plans and restrict some Medicaid and CHIP payments.

s2025-644.name: Senate Vote to Advance Health Care Cost Bill Fails
s2025-644.plain: The Senate voted 51 to 48 to end debate on the Lower Health Care Costs Act so it could move ahead, but this did not reach the 60 votes needed, so the bill is blocked for now. The bill would extend through 2028 the expanded eligibility and larger payments for the premium tax credit that help people pay for health insurance bought through exchanges.

s2025-645.name: Resolution to confirm a batch of nominations together
s2025-645.plain: The Senate voted 52 to 47 to approve a resolution that lets it consider several pending nominees for government posts as a single group rather than one at a time. All 52 Republicans voting supported it, and all 45 Democrats voting opposed it.

s2025-646.name: Senate Opens Debate on 2026 Defense Authorization Bill
